title: Throwing a stoneware French butter crock
subtitle: A two-piece butter keeper where a water seal in the base keeps butter fresh at room temperature
excerpt: A French butter crock (also called a butter bell) keeps a full block of butter at room temperature for weeks without refrigeration. The two-piece design , a deep cup that holds the butter and an outer well that holds a little cold water , creates a water seal that excludes air. Both pieces are thrown on the wheel and fitted together at leather-hard.
sourceNotes: Stoneware French butter crock throwing pattern derived from first principles.

content.text: Silica dust is the chronic studio hazard. Silicosis is irreversible. Mix wet whenever possible. Wear a P100 respirator any time raw glaze powders are open. Wet-clean only: no sweeping, no dry sanding indoors. Adequate ventilation when firing. Do not open a hot kiln below 80 degrees C.

The key dimension in a butter crock is the relationship between the butter cup flange and the well inside diameter. At bone-dry, the cup should drop into the well with 3-5 mm clearance on all sides , enough for the water seal, but close enough that the cup does not wobble when placed. This clearance must be planned at the throwing stage to account for clay shrinkage. Smooth stoneware typically shrinks 10-12% from wet to fired; calculate accordingly.

materials.name: Stoneware clay, smooth
materials.quantity: 300 g butter cup + 450 g outer well

materials.name: Mid-fire glaze, pre-mixed
materials.quantity: inside and outside both pieces, except base of well

content.text: Throw the butter cup

Wedge 300 g of smooth stoneware. Centre and throw a deep, straight-sided cup 70 mm in diameter and 65 mm tall. The cup should be narrow-mouthed: pull the walls to a fairly straight cylinder with very slight inward taper. The mouth diameter will be measured with calipers as the master dimension for the outer well.

At the rim of the cup, throw a small outward flange , a 6 mm ledge that extends horizontally from the rim. This flange sits on the top of the outer well and prevents the cup from falling into the well. Compress the flange with the rib.
Measure the flange outer diameter with calipers. This is dimension A. Wire off and set aside to dry to
leather-hard
Throw the outer well

Wedge 450 g. Throw a wide, shallow bowl 105 mm in diameter and 55 mm tall. The inner well diameter should match dimension A minus 6-8 mm (the clearance for the water seal). The walls should be straight or very slightly flared outward.
Create a small inward rim at the top of the well , a 5 mm step that prevents the butter cup flange from slipping. The butter cup should rest on this step, held loosely in place.

Check the fit at leather-hard by lowering the butter cup into the well. It should drop into the well with 3-5 mm clearance all round and rest on the inward rim step. Adjust if needed , the clearance will reduce slightly as both pieces dry further.
Trim foot-ring, bisque, and glaze
Trim a
foot-ring
on the outer well at leather-hard. Allow both pieces to dry to bone-dry.
Bisque
fire both pieces at
cone
06. Glaze both pieces fully inside and outside with the mop brush and glaze tongs for dipping. Leave only the foot-ring base bare. Glaze-fire to cone 6 (1220 degrees C).
Using the butter crock

Pack softened butter into the cup, pressing firmly to eliminate air pockets. Put 2-3 cm of cold water in the outer well. Invert the butter cup into the well , the water seals the butter from air. Change the water every two to three days. Butter keeps at room temperature for two to four weeks using this method.

rows.problem: Butter cup falls into the well , no support
rows.cause: The rim step was not deep enough, or the clearance between cup and well is too large
rows.fix: For the next piece, increase the rim step to 7-8 mm and reduce the clearance to 3 mm maximum.

rows.problem: Cup is too tight , cannot be removed from the well
rows.cause: Clearance was not enough at the throwing stage; firing brought the two pieces to matching dimensions
rows.fix: Check fit at leather-hard, before firing. If already fired and too tight, the pair cannot be adjusted.
